label: early-prefix bigram detector: input 2 or 3 is one of {x,e,g,0,z,f,o,r,n} after one of {f,0,x,r,e}
explanation: Fires almost only in the original phase at steps 1-3 (t=1: 53% of mass, t=2: 44%, t=3: 3%); never at t=0, never in copy phase, and only trivially at the delimiter. Within those steps it fires when the current and previous inputs both come from a small set of tokens: current input x or e (strongest), then g, 0, z, f, o, r, n; previous input f, 0, x, r or e. Strongest examples are 0 f [e] and 0 f [x] (about 1.0 of max), and f f [e/x] (about 0.95). Magnitude goes up with the strength of both tokens, and at t=1 it also depends on the first token (0 and f highest). Activation at t=3 is usually a weaker leftover after a strong t=2 step. It looks like a graded sum of the first few tokens contributions, so the token-set predicate is only an approximation: it misses weak activations on other pairs (e.g. f y, z g) and has false positives where the earlier context is weak (e.g. v f o).
